titulo: Hello, world!: Informal and formal dialogues

aula.objetivo: Greet people in any situation, recognise 13 new letters, say what your name is and tell formal from informal.

blocos.contexto: Two university classmates meet in the corridor.

linhas.pt: — Hi! I am Anton. And you?
— Nice to meet you! How are you?
— Yes, I am a student. And you?
— Nice to meet you too. Bye!

blocos.contexto: In the office, Сергей meets the director, Ирина Петровна, for the first time.

linhas.pt: — Hello! What is your name, madam?

linhas.ru: — Здравствуйте! Меня зовут Ирина Петровна. А вас?
linhas.pt: — Hello! My name is Irina Petrovna. And yours, sir?
linhas.audio: Здравствуйте! Меня зовут Ирина Петровна. А вас?

linhas.pt: — My name is Sergey. Nice to meet you.
— The pleasure is mine. How are you?
— Great, thank you. And you, madam?

blocos.titulo: How to say your name: «Меня зовут…»
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: To say your name, Russian literally says «me they call…». The ready-made sentence is «Меня зовут Лена» (mee-NYAH zah-VOOT LYEH-nah): «меня» is «me», «зовут» is «they call». Put your own name in place of «Лена». STEP 2: To ask a friend, say «Как тебя зовут?» (kahk tee-BYAH zah-VOOT). To ask someone who deserves respect, say «Как вас зовут?» (kahk vahs zah-VOOT). STEP 3: Notice: there is no word for «my», «is» or «am». The sentence is short and the name comes last, just as it is. STEP 4: After the name, the polite reply is «Очень приятно» (OH-cheen pree-YAHT-nah), «nice to meet you». The other person answers «Мне тоже» (mnyeh TOH-zheh), «me too». STEP 5: For now, learn «меня», «тебя» and «вас» as ready-made blocks. In lesson 14 you will see where these forms come from.
blocos.comparacao: in English you say «my name is» or «I am called». In Russian nobody says «I» or «my»: the sentence uses «me they call», and the name comes at the end.

exemplos.pt: What is your name? For a friend.

tabela.situation: With the boss or a stranger
tabela.question: Как вас зовут?

erros.motivo: The sentence does not start with «я». Russian says «меня зовут», «me they call».
The question uses «тебя», not «ты». It is a ready-made form.
To a teacher, a boss or a stranger, use «вас».

itens.explicacao: The sentence starts with «Меня зовут» and ends with the name «Лена» (LYEH-nah). With «Антон», the ending would be different.
In the middle of the question you heard «вас» (vahs), the formal form. With «тебя» it would be informal.
In the middle of the question you heard «тебя» (tee-BYAH), the informal form. With «вас» it would be formal.
It starts with «Я» (I) and ends in t, without «ка»: the speaker is a man.

itens.enunciado: You introduce yourself to a stranger. Which question asks for their name?
itens.explicacao: With a stranger you use the formal «вас». «Как дела?» asks how the person is, not their name.
«Меня зовут» is the formula for saying your own name. Then comes the name, unchanged.

itens.enunciado: Someone who says «Мне тоже приятно» is answering:
itens.explicacao: «Мне тоже» means «me too». It answers «nice to meet you».

itens.enunciado: How does Russian say «My name is Anton»?
itens.explicacao: The formula is fixed: «Меня зовут» and then the name. «Я зовут» does not exist.
You are talking about yourself, so you use «меня» (me). «тебя» and «вас» are forms for the other person.
To the teacher, who deserves respect, you use «вас».

itens.enunciado: — Здравствуйте! Как вас зовут? — Меня ___ Сергей.
itens.explicacao: The formula is «Меня зовут» and then the name. Without «зовут» the sentence is incomplete.
«Мне тоже» is the ready-made answer, «me too».

itens.enunciado: Put in order: «My name is Anton.»
itens.explicacao: The formula is fixed: «Меня зовут» and then the name, which comes last.

itens.enunciado: Put in order: «What is your name?» (formal)
itens.explicacao: The question starts with «Как» (how), then «вас» and finally «зовут».
Three words: «Меня», «зовут» and the name. The «я» in «меня» is a letter you will see in lesson 3.
Two words. The sign «ь» and the «я» arrive in lesson 3; for now, copy carefully what you hear.

itens.enunciado: Write in Russian what you say to your boss when meeting a new person: greet them, ask their name and say yours.
itens.respostaEsperada: Здравствуйте! Как вас зовут? Меня зовут Антон.

blocos.enunciado: Do both voices of the first dialogue, imitating the intonation, and then those of the second. Then swap «Лена» and «Антон» for your own name and answer «Как тебя зовут?» and «Как вас зовут?» aloud.
blocos.exemplo: Привет! Меня зовут Антон. Очень приятно!

blocos.enunciado: Write in Cyrillic 3 greetings you remember and 2 goodbyes.
